## Overnight

The tape is quiet with a modest overnight bid in equities (+0.18% SPX, +0.33% NDX) accompanied by a sharp VIX compression (-9.66%), though large-cap tech is fractionally underwater and the long end is flat to slightly higher—this appears to be positioning relief rather than directional conviction. The headline's assertion about a Fed rate hike lifting an "overhang" does not align with the data; more likely this is routine pre-cash consolidation ahead of today's session.

## The tape

Equities are mildly bid with tech leading at 29,562 on Nasdaq 100 futures, but the real story is in rates: the front end is selling off hard — the 2Y is up 7bp to 4.74% — while the 30Y is actually down 1bp at 5.35%, collapsing the 2s10s spread 6bp to +27bp and flattening the curve aggressively. Fed funds futures have repriced sharply, implying 4.16% by December versus a 3.75% spot, which means the market is now pricing roughly 40bp of hikes from here; that, combined with WTI crude sliding to $101.22 and gold holding at $4,345.90 with a softer dollar at 100.16, reads as a growth-scare-lite — inflation expectations being reanchored higher on the short end while the long end stays capped on demand concerns.

## Talking point of the day

> The curve is doing something specific right now: the 2Y is up 7bp on the day while the 30Y is actually down a basis point, compressing 2s10s by 6bp to +27bp in a single session — that bear-flattening move tells you the market believes the Fed has more work to do near-term but that longer-run growth doesn't justify pricing in sustained higher rates, which is exactly the dynamic that tends to pressure risk appetite in cyclicals and small caps even as Nasdaq holds a bid.
